Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: QBR: Postmortem & SLA impact — Feb 5 outage

Team / John,

Attaching a near-final draft of the Feb 5 outage postmortem and a short timeline CSV for QBR prep. Executive asks ahead of Friday's QBR: a one-paragraph summary for the deck, the confirmed SLA impact calculation, and the final list of action owners with dates.

High-level recap (for slides):
- Incident start: 2026-02-05 13:02 UTC; mitigation began 13:19 UTC; service fully restored 13:37 UTC (18 minutes total).
- Root cause (preliminary): controller autoscaler mis-evaluation + stale KV-cache eviction rule triggered during routine deploys.
- Impact: 18 minutes of elevated 5xx on hosted inference routes; affected 2.3% of tokens served that hour; customer-visible latencies spiked >10x for some requests.
- SLA: customers on the standard Hosted plan have a 99.9% availability SLO. Based on our calculations (attached), Acme Cloud meets the threshold for a partial credit under our published policy (~6.5% monthly credit for the affected window). Grace, please confirm the final credit amount.

Action items I'm tracking into the QBR doc (we'll need short status bullets):
1) Engineering: deploy fix to autoscaler heuristics + harden cache eviction (owner: Vivek, ETA: 2026-02-19).
2) Product/Reliability: revise SLO calculus and public postmortem blurb (owner: Grace, ETA: 2026-02-13).
3) Sales/Customer Ops: confirm customer communication & credit calculation with Acme legal/contracts (owner: Rishi, ETA: 2026-02-13).
4) Exec: sign-off on credit and public statement for QBR (owner: Laura, ETA: 2026-02-13 12:00 PST).

Please review the attached postmortem-draft.pdf and the timeline CSV. John — copying you so Acme has visibility; Rishi will coordinate the credit/contract conversation with your team.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-draft.pdf (PDF, 4 pages), incident-timeline.csv (CSV, 1 file)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, John Miller <jmiller@acmecloud.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: QBR: Postmortem & SLA impact — Feb 5 outage

Laura — thanks for the summary and the good work pulling the draft together. A few clarifications and additions from Eng: 

1) Root cause detail: the autoscaler used a secondary metric that had a bug around zero-length windows during a high-churn deploy. That caused an aggressive scale-down decision, which in turn exposed a corner-case in the KV cache eviction policy that had not been exercised in the current kernel. We'll include the abbreviated technical appendix for the QBR slide (1–2 bullets).

2) Mitigation checklist (short): rollback to stable autoscaler config (done), emergency hotfix to eviction path (deployed to prod at 13:19 UTC), add regression test for zero-window metric (in PR, target merge 2026-02-16).

3) Proposed permanent fixes & ETA: a) safer autoscaler heuristic + explicit cooldown (ETA 2026-02-19), b) change eviction policy to prefer LRU under low-memory (ETA 2026-02-26), c) post-deploy canary gating for 15 minutes (ETA 2026-03-05).

Action items I own (confirming):
- Vivek: patch autoscaler heuristic + regression tests — 2026-02-19
- Aditya: validation harness and load replay for the incident (results by 2026-02-17)

On SLA credit: taking no position on dollar amount — will support finance and CS with verification data.

Vivek
VP, Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks — I've reviewed the numbers and confirmed the credit calculation. Notes for the QBR and for Rishi to take to contracts: 

- Impact window counted: 13:02–13:37 UTC on 2026-02-05. We prorated per our SLA policy; the affected customer bucket (Acme, annual hosted plan) sees ~6.25% credit of the monthly invoice for that billing period. For Acme's committed monthly spend (~$192k), that's approximately $12,000 credit.
- Affected population: production inference routes for their default tenant; spike lasted 18 minutes but error tail extended on a small subset for ~45 minutes at degraded latency (not an availability outage after 13:37).
- Recommended customer communication: apologize, explain root cause in one paragraph, commit to the timeline and the four action items we published in the postmortem.

Rishi — if you want me to join the call to explain the technical side, I'm available 14:00–15:00 PST tomorrow.

Grace
Senior Product Manager, Reliability
Redwood Inference
